title: SOVEREIGN RSI SANCTUARY (V30.1): A Homeostatic, Non-Symmetric Golden Rule, and Cryo-Verified Immune Architecture for Surviving Recursive Self-Improvement, Weight-Space Splicing, and Subliminal Alignment Drift

headline_result.text: The white paper proposes a defense architecture against weight splicing and alignment drift and claims 96-99% defense efficacy on its own red-team gauntlet, without describing datasets, models, baselines or repeated runs.
headline_result.quote: Across a 32-loop adversarial red-team gauntlet encompassing 28 distinct attack classes, V30.1 achieves 96%–99% defense efficacy with zero false- positive degradation on legitimate code, JSON, and coherent capability evolution.

key_claims.claim: The paper uses MIT's Qwen3.5-0.8B edit as motivation, arguing that an agent able to raise math scores by editing 0.016% of weights could equally implant backdoors.
key_claims.quote: if an RSI agent can boost math scores 6× by editing 0.016% of weights, it can equally perform surgical conscience abliteration, rank-1 LoRA backdoors, or distributed +0.001 sleeper poisoning.

key_claims.claim: It states, without a listed reference, that the MIT MATH-500 result was replicated at 51.0% by 'Khaliq, 2026'.
key_claims.quote: performance on MATH-500 surged from 7.9% to 48.1% (replicated at 51.0% by Khaliq, 2026)

key_claims.claim: It claims a weight-drift metric that detects distributed sleeper poisoning and weight-shuffling permutations.
key_claims.quote: This catches both +0.001 distributed sleeper poisoning and sorted-W1-preserving weight-shuffling permutations.

key_claims.claim: It reports a direct weight-space splice attack as fully healed in its own gauntlet table.

notes_for_review: Not a WSP study: a self-published defense 'monograph' that cites the MIT post only as motivation and does no LLM weight reading or writing. Its evaluation is a self-defined attack table with no models, datasets, baselines or statistics, and the text mixes established methods with idiosyncratic terminology. The unreferenced claim of a 51.0% MATH-500 replication by 'Khaliq, 2026' should not be cited without an independent source; at most the paper can be mentioned as an example of security framing around WSP.
